rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet told Hamza al-Aslami he could fast or break his fast while travelling; al-Razi gives no grading.
rows.anchor: أن حمزة الأسلمي سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi objects that relying on the travel report to permit breaking the fast would let a solitary report abrogate the Quran, whose apparent wording requires fasting the remaining days.
rows.anchor: هذا يقتضي نسخ القرآن بخبر الواحد لأن ظاهر القرآن يقتضي وجوب صوم سائر الأيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After rejecting the preceding arguments, Razi relies on the following Quranic statement, fasting is better for you, to establish his position.
rows.anchor: فالاعتماد في إثبات المذهب على قوله تعالى بعد هذه الآية

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك وعثمان بن أبي أوفى والشافعي وأبو حنيفة ومالك والثوري وأبو يوسف ومحمد
rows.claim: Anas, Uthman ibn Abi Awfa, al-Shafi'i, Abu Hanifa, Malik, al-Thawri, Abu Yusuf, and Muhammad hold that fasting while travelling is better.
rows.anchor: قال أنس بن مالك وعثمان بن أبي أوفى الصوم أفضل وهو مذهب الشافعي وأبي حنيفة ومالك والثوري وأبي يوسف ومحمد

rows.speaker: ابن المسيب والشعبي والأوزاعي وأحمد وإسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn al-Musayyib, al-Sha'bi, al-Awza'i, Ahmad, and Ishaq hold that breaking the fast is better for a traveller.
rows.anchor: وقالت طائفة أفضل الأمرين الفطر وإليه ذهب ابن المسيب والشعبي والأوزاعي وأحمد وإسحاق

rows.speaker: فرقة ثالثة
rows.claim: A third group says the better option is whichever is easier for the individual.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة ثالثة : أفضل الأمرين أيسرهما على المرء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers the analogy that shortened prayer is better, and so breaking the fast should be better: some colleagues say completing prayer is better, though he calls that weak; fasting missed in Ramadan remains owed and its time virtue is lost, while neither applies to shortened prayer.
rows.anchor: قال : الإتمام أفضل إلا أنه ضعيف

words: يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلْعُسْرَ
rows.speaker: فرقة ثالثة
rows.claim: The third group's view is supported by God's statement that He intends ease, so a traveller should fast if fasting is easier and break the fast if that is easier.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : { يريد الله بكم اليسر ولا يريد بكم العسر

rows.speaker: علي وابن عمر والشعبي
rows.claim: Ali, Ibn Umar, and al-Sha'bi require making missed fasts up consecutively.
rows.anchor: فمذهب علي وابن عمر والشعبي أنه يقضيه متتابعا

rows.speaker: علي وابن عمر والشعبي
rows.claim: Their first argument is Ubayy's reading, which Razi cites in support of consecutive make-up fasting.
rows.anchor: أن قراءة أبي { فعدة من أيام

rows.speaker: علي وابن عمر والشعبي
rows.claim: Their second argument is that make-up fasting follows the pattern of performance, which is consecutive.
rows.anchor: أن القضاء نظير الأداء فلما كان الأداء متتابعا

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The other jurists recommend consecutive make-up fasts but allow separated days; since the verse uses an indefinite noun in an affirmative context, it leaves the days unrestricted.
rows.anchor: وقال الباقون : التتابع مستحب وإن فرق جاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the phrase is an indefinite noun in an affirmative context, it commands a number of make-up days equal to those missed without requiring consecutive days.
rows.anchor: نكرة في سياق الإثبات ، فيكون ذلك أمرا بصوم أيام

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة بن الجراح
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says God did not grant permission to break the fast in order to make the make-up fast burdensome: one may do the days consecutively or separately.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة بن الجراح أنه قال : إن الله لم يرخص

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A man asked the Prophet whether scattered make-up fasts sufficed; the Prophet compared them to paying a debt in installments and said God is more entitled to pardon. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وروي أن رجلا قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akhara is indeclinable because it combines plurality and irregular declension: it is the plural of ukhra, feminine of akhar, on the af'al pattern, normally used with min or the definite article.
rows.anchor: لا ينصرف لأنه حصل فيه سببان الجمع والعدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi's reading takes the opening as a prescription of fasting, followed by rulings for two categories of excused people: those wholly unable and those who can fast with hardship.
rows.anchor: ثم بين أحوال المعذورين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb 'can bear' is ordinarily used for someone who can perform an act only with some hardship.
rows.anchor: هذا اللفظ لا يستعمل إلا في حق من يقدر عليه مع ضرب من المشقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi favors the non-abrogation reading because less abrogation is preferable and there is no wording here that signals abrogation.
rows.anchor: معلوم أن النسخ كلما كان أقل كان أولى

words: يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلْعُسْرَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making the witnessing-Ramadan verse an abrogator would contradict the adjacent declaration that God intends ease, since this reading changes restrictive obligation to an option and reverses ease and hardship.
rows.anchor: ولو كانت الآية ناسخة لهذا لما كان

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi rejects al-Asamm's interpretation because this phrase is coordinated with the sick and traveller, and a conjunct should differ from what it is joined to.
rows.anchor: احتج القاضي رحمه الله في فساد قول الأصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi replies that the sick and travellers in the first phrase are wholly unable to fast, while those in the later phrase can fast; the categories differ, so al-Asamm's interpretation is not weak.
rows.anchor: المراد من المسافر والمريض المذكورين في الآية هما اللذان

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i argues that identifying the clause with the very old would make 'fasting is better' inappropriate, since that person cannot fast.
rows.anchor: لو كان المراد هو الشيخ الهرم لما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers that the elderly person could be able to fast with hardship; in that case fasting may be called better because more difficult worship earns more reward.
rows.anchor: هذا محمول على الشيخ الهرم الذي يطيق الصوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shahr derives from visibility or fame: the month is named for its clear appearance, and people need to know it to time debts, rites, fasting, and pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: الشهر مأخوذ من الشهرة يقال ،

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the month is named after the crescent because it is conspicuous and clear.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم سمي الشهر شهرا باسم الهلال

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Ramadan is one of God's names, so 'the month of Ramadan' means the month of God.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد : إنه اسم الله تعالى

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says not to say Ramadan came or went, but to say the month of Ramadan, because Ramadan is one of God's names; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil derives Ramadan from ramda', a pre-autumn rain that washes dust from the earth; by analogy, the month washes the community's bodies of sins and purifies hearts.
rows.anchor: ما نقل عن الخليل أنه من الرمضاء بسكون الميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another derivation is ramad, the heat of sun-scorched stones: the name evokes burning hunger and severe hardship; it was also called tabi' because it followed and distressed people.
rows.anchor: أنه مأخوذ من الرمض وهو حر الحجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation says the transferred month names were given from the seasons in which they fell, and Ramadan coincided with days of intense heat.
rows.anchor: لما نقلوا أسماء الشهور عن اللغة القديمة سموها بالأزمنة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet explains Ramadan as the month that burns God's servants' sins; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وقد روى عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari derives Ramadan from the verb for tempering a blade between stones until thin; weapons were tempered during this month for use.
rows.anchor: قولهم : رمضت النصل أرمضه رمضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Ramadan is God's name, the month shares it because sins disappear in God's mercy, or because they burn through the month's blessing.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى أن الذنوب تتلاشى في جنب رحمة الله

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i reads shahr in the nominative as a substitute for al-siyam: fasting prescribed for you means the month of Ramadan.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الكسائي أنه ارتفع على البدل من الصيام

rows.speaker: الفراء والأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Farra and al-Akhfash take the nominative as predicate of an omitted subject, replacing 'days': the counted days are the month of Ramadan.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الفراء والأخفش أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali allows shahr in the nominative as a subject with an omitted predicate: among the fasts prescribed is the fast of Ramadan.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي : إن شئت جعلته مبتدأ محذوف الخبر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some grammarians allow shahr as a subject whose predicate is the relative clause, 'in which the Quran was revealed.'
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : يجوز أن يكون بمبتدأ وخبره

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali prefers taking the relative clause as an adjective of shahr, which makes the command to fast the month explicit; using it as the predicate would only state that Quran was revealed then.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي : والأشبه أن يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the accusative, one analysis supplies an imperative: 'Fast the month of Ramadan.'
rows.anchor: أما قراءة النصب ففيها وجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second accusative analysis makes shahr a substitute for the counted days.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : على الإبدال من أيام معدودات

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf proposes that the accusative shahr is the object of 'that you fast.'
rows.anchor: وهذا الوجه ذكره صاحب ( الكشاف )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection to al-Kashshaf's parsing is that it separates the subject from its predicate with the long clause 'in which Quran was revealed ... is better,' an impermissible break between what functions as one unit.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذا التقدير يصير النظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God singled Ramadan out for fasting because He singled it out for the greatest sign of lordship, the Quran's revelation; fasting is a fitting great sign of servanthood.
rows.anchor: لما خص هذا الشهر بهذه العبادة بين العلة لهذا التخصيص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says fasting is among the strongest means of removing bodily attachments that veil divine light from human spirits; people of spiritual unveiling reach that light only through fasting.
rows.anchor: الصوم أقوى الأسباب في إزالة العلائق البشرية

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet is quoted saying that if satans did not hover around human hearts, people would see the kingdom of the heavens; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( لولا أن الشياطين يحومون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shared spiritual character of fasting and Quran revelation explains why the month that receives revelation is specifically assigned fasting.
rows.anchor: فثبت أن بين الصوم وبين نزول القرآن مناسبة عظيمة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet dates Abraham's scrolls to Ramadan's first night, the Torah to its sixth, the Gospel to its thirteenth, and the Quran to its twenty-fourth; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi raises the problem that the Quran came to Muhammad piecemeal over twenty-three years, with portions revealed in months other than Ramadan, so the verse needs explanation.
rows.anchor: أن القرآن ما نزل على محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام دفعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first answer is that the entire Quran descended on Laylat al-Qadr to the lowest heaven, then came down to earth gradually; this arrangement may have benefited the angels, the Prophet, or Gabriel.
rows.anchor: أن القرآن أنزل في ليلة القدر جملة إلى سماء الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi refers to his explanation of why revelation was gradual at Quran 25:32, where disbelievers ask why it was not sent all at once.
rows.anchor: شرحناها في سورة الفرقان في تفسير قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq's second answer is that revelation began on Laylat al-Qadr in Ramadan; beginnings of religions and states mark history because they are noble and occur at known, fixed times.
rows.anchor: وهو قول محمد بن إسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi prefers the first answer because it needs no figurative interpretation; Ibn Ishaq's answer requires taking 'the Quran' to mean only some of its parts.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الجواب الأول لا يحتاج فيه إلى تحمل شيء من المجاز

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar infers from this verse and Quran 97:1 that Laylat al-Qadr must fall in Ramadan: revelation on that night is therefore revelation in Ramadan, just as a month can be clarified by specifying its day.
rows.anchor: روي أن ابن عمر استدل بهذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account is that the entire Quran descended from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven on Laylat al-Qadr, then was sent to Muhammad gradually through the end of his life.
rows.anchor: إن الله تعالى أنزل كل القرآن من اللوح المحفوظ إلى السماء الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account is that each year portions needed by Muhammad and his community were sent from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven, then revealed to the Prophet as needed.
rows.anchor: كان ينزل من اللوح المحفوظ إلى السماء الدنيا من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says both accounts are possible, since 'Ramadan' may denote a particular month or the kind of month; he therefore suspends judgment.
rows.anchor: كلاهما محتمل ، وذلك لأن قوله

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة والحسين بن الفضل
rows.claim: Sufyan ibn Uyayna, a view chosen by al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl, interprets the phrase as saying that the Quran was revealed concerning Ramadan's virtue.
rows.anchor: قال سفيان بن عيينة : أنزل فيه القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari interprets 'in Ramadan' as referring to Quranic revelation about the obligation to fast it, as in saying that revelation 'in' zakat concerns its obligation.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري : أنزل في إيجاب صومه على الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quran is the name for God's speech contained between the two covers.
rows.anchor: القرآن اسم لما بين الدفتين من كلام الله

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i says Quran is a proper, unhamzated name for God's Book, not derived from qara'a, like Torah and Gospel; qira'ah is hamzated.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن عبد الله بن الحكم أن الشافعي رضي الله عنه كان يقول

rows.speaker: القائلون بالاشتقاق من قرن
rows.claim: Some who derive the unhamzated form connect it with qarn, joining: the Quran joins its suras, verses, and letters, its rulings and wisdom, or evidences of its divine origin, including eloquence, unique style, unseen reports, and abundant knowledge.
rows.anchor: أنه مأخوذ من قرنت الشيء بالشيء

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra suggests the name comes from qarā'in, indicators, because the Quran's verses corroborate one another, as Quran 4:82 says a non-divine book would contain many inconsistencies.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : أظن أن القرآن سمي من القرائن

rows.speaker: القائلون بالهمز
rows.claim: Those who hamz the name derive it from qara'a, recitation, a verbal noun; an anonymous poetic line uses قرآنا to mean recitation, and the recited object can take its verbal noun as a name.
rows.anchor: وأما الذين همزوا فلهم وجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi cites Quran 17:78's wording as an example in his account of the Quran's name.
rows.anchor: أقم الصلواة لدلوك الشمس إلى

rows.speaker: الزجاج وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj and Abu Ubayda derive Quran from qar', gathering, because it collects and joins the suras.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج وأبو عبيدة : إنه مأخوذ من القرء وهو الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi glosses Amr's line: taqra' means she has not gathered a fetus in her womb, illustrating qar' as gathering.
rows.anchor: أي لم تجمع في رحمها ولدا

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub says Quran is what the reciter casts from his mouth, drawing on an Arab expression about a camel that has not expelled its afterbirth; the related term also names menstruation.
rows.anchor: قول قطرب وهو أنه سمي قرآنا

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub supports his derivation with the saying 'the camel has never expelled a fetus membrane': just as the animal casts something out, the reciter casts the Quran from his mouth.
rows.anchor: قول قطرب وهو أنه سمي قرآنا ، لأن القارىء يكتبه ، وعند القراءة كأنه يلقيه من فيه أخذا من قول العرب : ما قرأت الناقة سلى قط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi distinguishes tanzil as gradual descent from inzal as descent all at once, citing Quran 2:23 and 3:3; this supports taking the verse's inzal as the Quran's descent from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven, which he prefers over other explanations.
rows.anchor: التنزيل مختص بالنزول على سبيل التدريج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi refers back to Quran 2:2, where the Quran is guidance for the God-fearing, to reconcile that description with calling it guidance for all people here.
rows.anchor: بينا تفسير الهدى في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusatives 'guidance for people' and 'clear proofs' are circumstantial: God sent the Quran down as guidance to truth and manifest signs that guide to truth and distinguish truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: نصب على الحال ، أي أنزل وهو هداية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To explain the apparent repetition, Razi says the verse first names guidance generally, then singles out its clearest and best form: manifest guidance that distinguishes truth from falsehood, as emphasis.
rows.anchor: هذا من باب ما يذكر الجنس ويعطف نوعه عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation is that the Quran is guidance itself and also contains guidance from earlier books, the Torah and Gospel, which were themselves guidance and criterion; Razi cites 3:3-4, 2:53, and 21:48.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالهدى والفرقان : التوراة والإنجيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation removes repetition by assigning the first guidance to fundamentals of religion and the later guidance to derivative rulings.
rows.anchor: فحينئذ يزول التكرار والله أعلم

rows.speaker: الأخفش والمازني
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash and al-Mazini call the fa in 'whoever witnesses the month, let him fast it' extra, seeing no coordinating or conditional role for it.
rows.anchor: عن الأخفش والمازني أنهما قالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the fa is conditional: because Ramadan has special virtue, it appropriately receives a special act of worship, making the prior account of its virtue relevant.
rows.anchor: وأقول : يمكن أن يقال الفاء ههنا للجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the fa in Quran 62:8 is not extra either; it marks the consequence that those who flee death have death brought near, showing caution cannot avert fate.
rows.anchor: الفاء فيه غير زائدة وأيضا بل هذا من باب مقابلة الضد بالضد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shahida means to be present; shuhud means presence.
rows.anchor: شهد } أي حضر والشهود الحضور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first analysis, the object of shahida is omitted, meaning the town or home; al-shahr is a temporal adverb and the pronoun in falyasumhu refers to it, so the sense is whoever is present and not travelling.
rows.anchor: أن مفعول شهد محذوف لأن المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the second analysis, al-shahr itself is the object: whoever apprehends the month with knowledge should fast it, as in saying one witnessed someone's era.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : مفعول { شهد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi prefers the second analysis by the legal-theory principle that when ellipsis and specification conflict, specification is preferable; the first requires both an omitted object and exclusions, while the second needs only exclusions for children, the insane, and the ill.
rows.anchor: متى وقع التعارض بين التخصيص والإضمار فالتخصيص أولى

rows.speaker: الواحدي وصاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Despite Razi's preference for the second parse, most leading scholars, including al-Wahidi and al-Kashshaf, adopt the first analysis with an omitted object.
rows.anchor: كالواحدي وصاحب ( الكشاف ) ذهبوا إلى الأول
